Tests {@link UnicodeEscaper}.

Every test escapes the same five-character sample {@value #SAMPLE}. Each letter has a fixed Unicode code point, so it is easy to predict which letters a given factory method escapes and what the resulting {@code \\uXXXX} sequences look like:

 letter | code point | escape sequence -------+------------+---------------- A | 0x41 | \\u0041 D | 0x44 | \\u0044 F | 0x46 | \\u0046 G | 0x47 | \\u0047 Z | 0x5A | \\u005A

An escaper only rewrites the letters it decides to escape; every other letter is copied through unchanged.
Sample translated by every test; see the class Javadoc for each letter's code point.
above('F') escapes code points strictly greater than 'F' (0x46), so only G (0x47) and Z (0x5A) are escaped; A, D and F pass through.
below('F') escapes code points strictly less than 'F' (0x46), so only A (0x41) and D (0x44) are escaped; F, G and Z pass through.
between('F', 'L') escapes code points in the inclusive range [0x46, 0x4C], so only F (0x46) and G (0x47) are escaped; A, D and Z fall outside the range.
